references.text: The people call Jesus 'the Prophet' whom God promised to raise up from among their own brothers, a direct fulfillment of the prophecy in Deuteronomy about a prophet who will be like Moses.
In John 1:21, the people ask the same question about whether Jesus is 'the Prophet,' showing that this expectation was widespread and that Jesus was identified with this role in several contexts.
After the bread miracle, the people express the same belief: 'This is truly the Prophet who was to come into the world,' a direct parallel to the confession in John 7:40.
Peter refers to Jesus as 'the Prophet' whom Moses spoke about, linking this title directly to Deuteronomy 18, which is the theological background for the people's statement in John 7:40.
In his speech before the Sanhedrin, Stephen calls Jesus 'the Prophet' that Moses foretold, confirming that Jesus is the one whom the people in John 7:40 believe him to be.
